name: Script Opposition
description: A setup activates one interpretation, then the punchline reveals a compatible opposing script.
rewrite_moves: name the assumed script before the punchline
make the second script arrive at the last content word
preserve compatibility between both interpretations
risk_notes: fails when the second script is random or unresolved

name: False Analogy
description: Treats two things as equivalent in a way that is locally legible but logically strained.
rewrite_moves: map the serious topic onto a mundane process
keep one shared property and exaggerate the mismatch
make the analogy collapse in the punchline
risk_notes: can become misinformation if the analogy implies a false factual claim

name: Wordplay / Pun
description: Uses sound, spelling, ambiguity, or double meaning as the turn.
rewrite_moves: identify a keyword with a second sense or sound neighbor
keep the setup short enough that the wordplay lands
avoid explaining the pun after it lands
risk_notes: often weak for audiences that dislike groan-heavy humor

name: Misdirection / Reversal
description: Guides the audience toward one expectation, then flips the direction at the end.
rewrite_moves: hide the turn until the last phrase
replace a generic ending with a specific reversed object
cut setup clauses that reveal the reversal early
risk_notes: can feel manipulative if the setup withholds essential information unfairly

name: Rule Of Three / AAB
description: Builds two matching beats, then makes the third beat deviate.
rewrite_moves: make beats one and two structurally parallel
make beat three shorter or more specific
put the strongest concrete noun in the third beat
risk_notes: too many beats dull the expectation

name: Callback / Tag
description: Reuses a previous joke object after the audience has learned its comic meaning.
rewrite_moves: reuse the strongest image from the prior laugh
shorten the callback compared with the original
tag only after laughter has peaked
risk_notes: callbacks fail when the original joke did not land

name: Specificity / Concreteness
description: Makes a joke funnier by replacing abstract labels with vivid objects, roles, or actions.
rewrite_moves: replace abstract nouns with visible objects
name a role, place, or tiny behavior
make the punchline imageable
risk_notes: over-specific references can exclude audiences without shared context

name: Hyperbole / Understatement
description: Scales a normal fact absurdly up or down.
rewrite_moves: exaggerate only one dimension
keep the emotional truth recognizable
use understatement after a high-stakes setup
risk_notes: can become bad surprise if exaggeration attacks a protected audience model

name: Anthropomorphism
description: Gives human motives to tools, systems, animals, or abstractions.
rewrite_moves: give the system one petty human desire
make the motive bureaucratic or emotionally familiar
avoid implying false technical claims
risk_notes: can blur factual understanding if framed as literal capability

name: Status Inversion
description: Makes the high-status actor or system briefly low-status.
rewrite_moves: target a process or role rather than voter identity
make the powerful thing reveal a petty weakness
keep the audience out of the butt position unless requested
risk_notes: political and workplace audiences can read this as identity attack if target is too broad

name: Shared Frustration
description: Turns a widely felt irritation into a shared comic object.
rewrite_moves: choose a frustration both sides recognize
target the friction instead of the group
make the audience feel seen before surprising them
risk_notes: fails if only one subgroup recognizes the frustration

name: Self-Deprecation
description: Places the speaker, not the audience, in the vulnerable comic position.
rewrite_moves: make the flaw low-stakes and specific
avoid making the speaker seem incompetent in a critical context
pivot from self-target to shared insight
risk_notes: repeated self-defeating humor can lower perceived confidence

name: Irony / Sarcasm
description: Says one thing while intending a contrasting stance that must be inferred from context.
rewrite_moves: make the intended stance recoverable
add context before the ironic line
avoid sarcasm for low-context or mixed audiences
risk_notes: high bad-surprise risk when the audience cannot infer stance

name: Bathos / Anti-Joke
description: Sets up importance and ends with a deliberately mundane or anticlimactic resolution.
rewrite_moves: inflate the setup, then end with a tiny literal detail
signal playful form-breaking if audience tolerance is low
use sparingly inside a set
risk_notes: can read as simply unfunny if audience expects conventional punchlines
